ns0:a.ns1:title: G.1 (I.cn.1): Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another.
G.2 (I.def.15): A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying within the figure are equal to one another ;

G.6 (I.cn.3): If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal.

G.8 (I.2): To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.

G.22 (I.13): If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.
G.23 (I.post.4): That all right angles are equal to one another.

G.25 (I.15): If two straight lines cut one another, they make the vertical angles equal to one another.

G.29 (I.18): In any triangle the greater side subtends the greater angle.
G.30 (I.19): In any triangle the greater angle is subtended by the greater side.
G.31 (I.20): In any triangle two sides taken together in any manner are greater than the remaining one.

G.38 (I.def.23): Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet one another in either direction.
G.39 (I.27): If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

G.47 (I.34): In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.
G.48 (I.35): Parallelograms which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another.
G.50 (I.37): Triangles which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another.
G.54 (I.41): If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the parallelogram is double of the triangle.

G.443 (XI.1): A part of a straight line cannot be in the plane of reference and a part in a plane more elevated.
G.444 (XI.2): If two straight lines cut one another, they are in one plane, and every triangle is in one plane.
G.445 (XI.3): If two planes cut one another, their common section is a straight line.
G.446 (XI.def.3): A straight line is at right angles to a plane, when it makes right angles with all the straight lines which meet it and are in the plane.

G.451 (XI.8): If two straight lines be parallel, and one of them be at right angles to any plane, the remaining one will also be at right angles to the same plane.
